# Steps `dev/ci_contract.py` permits to name a tool, and the reason each does.
#
# An entry is `workflow.yml:Step name`, or a bare `workflow.yml` for a lane
# whose conversion has not started. Every line is a debt with an owner, not a
# dispensation: the file exists so the unconverted surface is a number someone
# can burn down instead of a silence.
#
# TWO CLASSES ONLY.
#
#   runner-plane   Acts on the MACHINE, not the product. It has no meaning on
#                  a laptop, so there is no recipe it could be hiding. These
#                  belong in the shared runner tooling, which already owns
#                  the job hooks and the preflight; they are listed here
#                  until that render exists rather than pretended away.
#
#   pending        Product-plane work that SHOULD be a recipe and is not yet.
#                  Each names the recipe it is waiting for.

# --- runner-plane -----------------------------------------------------------
# Reclaims a workspace a killed job left root-owned, before checkout is the
# step that would hit EACCES. The runner fleet's job-completed hook cannot
# help: this has to run BEFORE the next job's checkout, not after the last
# job's end.
ci.yml:Reclaim the workspace from a job that may not have finished
merge-gate.yml:Reclaim the workspace from a job that may not have finished
code-health.yml:Reclaim the workspace from a job that may not have finished
release-please.yml:Reclaim the workspace from a job that may not have finished

# Fails the merge verdict for a fork's pull request, before anything is checked
# out. A statement about which code may merge; it has no local meaning.
merge-gate.yml:Refuse fork pull requests

# Folds the run's own job results (`needs`) and the head commit's earlier gate
# conclusion into the one required check. Both inputs exist only inside a
# workflow run, so there is no recipe it could be.
merge-gate.yml:Decide the merge verdict

# Reads engine/rust-toolchain.toml so the pin can be passed to
# dtolnay/rust-toolchain, which otherwise exports RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN and
# overrides the file. Feeds a `uses:`, so it cannot be a recipe.
merge-gate.yml:Read pinned toolchain
release-please.yml:Read pinned toolchain

# Absorbs a transient `socket hang up` from the toolchain action, which does
# not retry. Machine-level, idempotent, `|| true`.
merge-gate.yml:Warm the pinned toolchain, retrying a dropped connection
release-please.yml:Warm the pinned toolchain, retrying a dropped connection

# Names the shared cargo target directory for later steps, and repairs a
# runner whose sccache port has been squatted. Both write GITHUB_ENV; both are
# statements about this machine.
merge-gate.yml:Resolve the engine build output directory
merge-gate.yml:Verify the compile cache cannot block the gate

# Stops a `vaultspec serve` this job started and reports free space. The
# runner fleet's job-completed hook bounds DISK on both platforms; it does
# not kill processes.
merge-gate.yml:Reclaim runner disk (always)
merge-gate.yml:Reclaim runner disk (always · unix)
merge-gate.yml:Reclaim runner disk (always · windows)

# --- pending ----------------------------------------------------------------
# Puts vaultspec-core on PATH for the live-engine and e2e tiers. `just init`
# already installs it INTO the environment; the PATH export is what
# `init-tools` should absorb, which retires both of these.
merge-gate.yml:Install vaultspec-core (live-engine declared-tier dependency)
merge-gate.yml:Put vaultspec-core on PATH for the e2e tier

# Calls `just test-frontend`, but through a capture so the classifier below it
# has the log even when the runner dies mid-suite. Retired by teaching the
# recipe to write the log itself (VAULTSPEC_CI_REPORTS is the seam).
merge-gate.yml:Unit tests (just test-frontend)
merge-gate.yml:Say which kind of red this is

# The live-engine conformance lane: spawn a real serve over the fixture vault,
# run one vitest file against it, stop it. Recipe needed: `test-conformance`,
# with the spawn/poll/teardown in dev/ where it can run locally.
merge-gate.yml:Create fixture and start serve
merge-gate.yml:Run TS conformance test
merge-gate.yml:Stop serve

# Release-input gates. Recipe needed: `check-release-inputs`.
merge-gate.yml:Component lock + release-set-manifest schema are well-formed
merge-gate.yml:The committed Cargo.lock agrees with Cargo.toml
merge-gate.yml:Product builder, manifest verifiers, and lock/capsule/release pins
release-please.yml:Regenerate and push engine/Cargo.lock

# --- pending, whole lane ----------------------------------------------------
# The release and channel lanes: ~2,500 lines of inline bash and pwsh across
# the fleet, of which these are the dashboard's share. Nothing here can be run
# by a developer, which is why a release-path break surfaces at release. Each
# needs its own recipe set before its entry can be removed; they are named by
# file because converting one step of a lane in isolation buys nothing.
release.yml            # cargo-dist orchestration; recipes: build-release-*
product-release.yml    # release orchestrator: gate, compose/verify/attach, publish, promote
a2a-product-contract.yml       # reaches into vaultspec-a2a's build_binary.py
a2a-product-certification.yml  # per-target certification, four platforms
a2a-channel-feasibility.yml    # Scoop/WinGet install-upgrade-uninstall proofs
channel-publish-gate.yml
homebrew-bump.yml
scoop-bump.yml
winget-publish.yml
acquisition.yml        # recipe: test-acquisition, shared with core and rag
ci-runner-probe.yml    # runner-plane in full; belongs in the shared runner tooling
